title: Brownian Motion in Orthogonal and Symplectic Groups
abstract: Matrix Brownian motion provides a powerful framework for studying crossover ensembles in quantum chaos and quantum transport, as well as thermalization and information scrambling in many-body dynamics. Here, we develop a unified diagrammatic framework to characterize Brownian ensembles for orthogonal and symplectic random matrices, which describe systems with particle-hole symmetry. We compute polynomial averages up to fourth order and construct an orthogonally invariant interpolation for the disconnected $\mathrm{SO}^-(q)$ sector of the orthogonal group. We consider applications relating to the fields of quantum information, quantum chaos, and quantum transport.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive diagrammatic framework to analyze Brownian motion on orthogonal and symplectic random matrices. It calculates moment operators up to the fourth order, providing explicit mathematical tools for studying quantum chaos and transport phenomena in systems with particle-hole symmetry. The results are valuable for understanding spectral properties in complex many-body quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified diagrammatic framework to characterize Brownian ensembles for orthogonal and symplectic random matrices, which are used to study systems with particle-hole symmetry.
main_result: It provides explicit calculations for polynomial averages (moment operators) up to the fourth order ($k=4$) for these non-unitary matrix dynamics, establishing recurrence relations based on tensor algebra.
method: The authors use a diagrammatic approach to calculate time evolution operators $U_k(t) = e^{L_k t}$ and trace moments by expanding in powers of the coupling constant or time parameter.
model_or_system: The study concerns matrix Brownian motion on orthogonal ($O(q)$) and symplectic ($Sp(q)$) groups, relevant for quantum chaos, quantum transport, and many-body dynamics exhibiting particle-hole symmetry. The evolution is governed by random Hermitian matrices constrained by an antiunitary involution.
key_observables: Polynomial averages $\langle U_{k} i_1 \dots i'_k angle$, moment operators $U_k(t)$, and trace moments $R_{i_1, \dots, i_m}(t)$.
important_parameters: The order of the moment ($k$), system size ($q$), and time ($t$). The long-time limit converges to Haar-distributed ensembles.
main_assumptions: Calculations rely on defining basis tensors ($I_k, S_k, X_k$) whose multiplication rules are derived diagrammatically; some results assume invariance under transformations between $SO(q)$ and $O(q)$.
figures_summary: Figures 1 & 2 show the diagrammatic representations and multiplication rules for basis tensors ($I_2, S_2, X_2$) in both orthogonal and symplectic cases. Further figures illustrate higher-rank tensor diagrams.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the framework for calculating moment operators $U_k(t)$ diagrammatically (up to $k=4$). It details the algebra of basis tensors, calculates explicit forms for $U_2(t)$, $U_3(t)$, and finally provides complex analytical expressions for $U_4(t)$ and associated trace moments.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends random matrix theory techniques (originally developed for unitary ensembles) to systems with specific symmetries like particle-hole symmetry, which are crucial in condensed matter physics (e.g., superconductors).
